text:
maria (eng-security): FYI a DSAR deletion for user uid:12345 failed during our keystore step. KMS re-encrypt returned 404 for a snapshot key :disappointed:

aj (eng-platform): ugh, do we have logs? which step failed — decrypt, rewrap, or revoke?

maria (eng-security): paste of the relevant log snippet:```
2025-05-14T16:07:12Z ERROR dsar-service deleteFlow uid=12345 step=keystore_reencrypt error="re-encrypt failed: ciphertext not found (snapshots/2025/uid-12345)"
2025-05-14T16:07:12Z INFO dsar-service marking uid=12345 status=pending_deletion reason="keystore_reencrypt_failure"
```

samir (sre): :eyes: that ciphertext path is from our nightly snapshot pipeline. If a snapshot is immutable and still referenced we can't fully delete the object until snapshot GC runs. Are we sure GC didn't keep a reference?

maria (eng-security): confirmed snapshot exists in gs://redwood-backups/2025-05-13/snap-uid-12345. KMS key id = projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/kr-main/cryptoKeys/ck-snap-v1. Deleting requires rewrap with active key or key be available. The re-encrypt call fails because the snapshot ciphertext ID isn't in keystore index. looks like a metadata drift between snapshot service and keystore indexing.

lina (legal): hold on — legal wants a preservation hold until we confirm scope of data and any open litigation flags. Can you open a retention-exception ticket? we need chain-of-custody.

maria (eng-security): Opening ticket now: RE-2025-314 retention-exception request. Propose short-term plan: 1) mark record pending_deletion in user-store (already done), 2) create retention exception (legal) to avoid automated purge, 3) kick off keystore index reconciliation job, 4) once keystore has ciphertext indexed re-attempt re-encrypt and delete snapshots.

aj (eng-platform): Question: current delete flow uses service account svc-dsar-writer which lacks keystore-read for snapshot namespace. We can either grant svc-dsar-writer temporary keystore access (RBAC change) or have a keystore-proxy job with minimal permissions to reconcile. I'm leaning to proxy + short-lived token to avoid expanding svc principal perms permanently.

samir (sre): proxy + short-lived token sounds safer. We need to ensure the proxy emits audit events for every key access so legal can prove who touched what. Also add tracing span so oncall can correlate.

ops-oncall (oncall): also note deploy-bot rolled out keystore v2 last week. There were a couple of index migrations that had soft-failures. Can we check deploy logs?

deploy-bot: rollout keystore-v2 completed 2025-05-10T02:13:11Z. Migration job mg-idx-20250510 exited with code 0 but 27 objects reported mismatch and wrote to /var/log/migrations/mg-idx-20250510-mismatch.log.

maria (eng-security): ok that matches. Action items: - aj: implement keystore-proxy runbook (short-lived token, proxy logs to audit-log, minimal scope) - samir: add trace span and ensure oncall alert if re-encrypt fails >3x - ops-oncall: pull migration mismatch log and flag any uid-namespace matches to escalate - lina: confirm retention-exception form + required legal fields for chain-of-custody - maria: run a reconciliation pass and requeue failed DSAR deletions once keystore index fixed.

aj (eng-platform): I'll prototype the proxy this afternoon. rough interface: POST /proxy/rewrap {ciphertext_path, target_key} -> returns status and audit_event_id. We'll use short-lived tokens minted by our token-service with ttl 10m. Also will write audit event: type=dsar_keystore_rewrap, actor=svc-dsar-proxy, request_id=<uuid>.

lina (legal): For retention-exception we need: requester identity stamp, case id (RE-2025-314), reason, hold owner, expected retention_end (if any), and statement that deletion attempt occurred and failed due to keystore/migration. Please cc privacy@redwood on the ticket.

samir (sre): one more: if we can't re-encrypt due to missing key material (KMS key disabled/deleted) we need a forensics escalation path. That includes snapshot export for legal review and a signed manifest (hash) of files we couldn't decrypt. Can security own that runbook?

maria (eng-security): yes security will own forensic manifest flow. We'll add a step to produce a signed manifest with sha256 per object and store it in secure evidence bucket with restricted ACLs.

ops-oncall (oncall): to avoid future drift let's add an integration test on the snapshot pipeline: after snapshot creation, immediately verify keystore index entry exists and rewrap test ciphertext with the intended key. fail the pipeline if mismatch. low effort but catches this early.

aj (eng-platform): agreed. Adding a CI check to snapshot job. Also will add a one-off job to reconcile index for 2025-05-10..2025-05-14 windows. estimate 2 hours.

maria (eng-security): thanks all. I'll update the retention-exception ticket and ping privacy + infra once proxy PR is up. If anyone sees additional UIDs in the mismatch log, drop them in RE-2025-314. :thumbsup:

lina (legal): acknowledged. please include audit_event_id for each attempted rewrap in the ticket.

aj (eng-platform): will do. tagging this thread for follow-up in #eng-platform after proxy PR.

samir (sre): adding a short-term oncall play: if DSAR delete fails with re-encrypt error, ops-oncall should open an incident stub and add label "dsar-keystore-failure" so legal and sec can track.

maria (eng-security): done. closing loop for now — will re-open when reconciliation completes or if legal requests evidence. thanks.
